summary: Carney signs a new partnership with Turkiye as Canada looks beyond the US, Toronto votes Monday in a tight race, and a rate decision comes Wednesday.
body: Prime Minister Mark Carney finished a three-day visit to Turkiye on Saturday, the first bilateral visit there by a Canadian prime minister [^1]. He and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan agreed a new strategic partnership on defence and energy, with free-trade talks expected in the coming weeks, plus an air agreement that could nearly double direct flights [^1]. The trip is part of Carney's push to sell to more countries and depend less on the United States [^1]. Asked about doing business with governments that do not share Canada's values, he said "engagement is not approval"; Turkiye faces criticism over a crackdown on LGBTQ+ rights, and Carney said Canada raised human rights in its talks [^1].

Toronto and other Ontario cities vote on Monday, Oct. 26. Olivia Chow, the incumbent mayor, and former councillor Brad Bradford made final pitches across the city on Saturday in a race CTV describes as tighter than ever [^2]. Polls released last week differed depending on the pollster [^3].

On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the Bank of Canada announces its next interest rate decision. In a Reuters poll, 19 of 34 economists expect a rise from 2.25% to 2.50%, its first move in a year, while the rest expect no change [^4]. Inflation was 3.1% in September, just above the Bank's 1% to 3% target range, and oil prices have climbed further since [^5]. A hike would make loans and mortgages a little more expensive. It was otherwise a quiet weekend in federal politics.
differences: Most economists polled expect a rate hike, but 15 of 34 expect none, citing a weak economy [^4].
